title: The power of expectation
text: Sugar pills contain no medicine, yet when patients believe in them, real things happen in the body. This is the placebo effect, and it is more than imagination: brain scans show genuine {{1}} in pain pathways, and symptoms from nausea to depression measurably improve. The effect is strongest where the problem is {{2}} produced by the nervous system — pain, fatigue, sickness — and weakest against tumours and broken bones, which no amount of belief can set. Expectation does much of the work, but a {{3}} manner in the consulting room contributes too: studies find that a warm, confident consultation is itself a mild treatment. Curiously, placebos keep working even when people know exactly what they are taking, a finding that has {{4}} the old rule that an inert pill must be disguised. Placebos also have a dark {{5}}: warn patients convincingly about side effects and they will develop them, at rates that {{6}} every clinical trial. Ethics committees therefore {{7}} with awkward questions — if belief is a treatment, is it right to {{8}} it deliberately? For patients, though, the message is simpler: the mind is not a spectator at its own illness.

gaps.explanation: 'genuine changes in pain pathways' — measurable alterations; habits, rituals and routines are not what brain scans show.
'largely produced by the nervous system' — mostly; widely means in many places, and greatly and hugely describe degree, not share.
'a reassuring manner' — the manner reassures others, so the -ing participle; 'reassured' would mean the manner itself feels calm.
'has undermined the old rule' — weakened its authority; underline = emphasise, underestimate = judge too low, undergo = experience.
'placebos have a dark side' — the fixed expression for a negative aspect; slope, shade and shelf do not form this idiom.
'at rates that complicate every clinical trial' — make it harder to interpret; comply takes 'with', imply and certify do not fit the meaning.
'grapple with awkward questions' — wrestle with them; grope takes 'for', gamble with money or safety, not questions.
'is it right to cultivate it deliberately' — encourage the growth of a belief; the other verbs share a similar form but none means foster.
